title: Two Former FBI Officials Charged with Lying to Congress Over Hunter Biden Investigation
snippet: Federal prosecutors have charged former FBI officials Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides with making false statements to Congress regarding the Hunter Biden probe, drawing sharp pushback from defense attorneys who call the charges politically motivated.
content:
WASHINGTON — Two former senior FBI officials who previously managed election security and counterintelligence operations have been criminally charged with lying to Congress about their roles in the probe into Hunter Biden, according to federal court records unsealed Friday.

The criminal complaint names Nikki Floris, former deputy assistant director of the FBI’s Counterintelligence Division, and Bradley Benavides, a former senior FBI official who focused on foreign influence and election threats. Both face a single count of making false statements to lawmakers—a charge that carries significant legal hurdles for prosecutors.

Defense Teams Decry 'Political' Prosecution

U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia Jeanine Pirro announced on social media that both defendants surrendered to authorities Friday morning, alleging they lied under oath regarding their activities within the FBI's Foreign Influence Task Force and the broader Hunter Biden investigations.

Defense attorneys for both former officials delivered a blistering response to the charges, characterizing them as a weaponization of the Justice Department aimed at settling political scores.

"The DOJ has accused her falsely of a crime on the say-so of politicians, not on the facts," Floris’s legal team said in a statement, highlighting her nearly 20-year career as a dedicated intelligence officer. "It’s no coincidence the government is filing these nonsense charges now."

Ronald S. Safer, an attorney representing Benavides, echoed those sentiments, calling the filing a "disgrace" against a public servant who spent two decades defending the nation against foreign intelligence threats and terrorism.

Under the Microscope in Washington

The case against Floris and Benavides was brought via a criminal complaint rather than a grand jury indictment. Federal prosecutors in D.C. may face headwinds securing an indictment, as local grand juries have recently shown skepticism toward high-profile cases brought during the current administration.

Floris, who served as the FBI's security lead during the 2020 presidential election, has long drawn scrutiny from Congressional Republicans over internal emails and intelligence reporting handling. Her legal team maintained that all actions taken during her tenure followed standard administrative protocols for evaluating unverified intelligence.
